accepted_impacts.label: default catalog selection for new Databricks sessions
accepted_impacts.llm_reason: Changes to the execution-context constructor, together with changes to context creation and default-catalog methods, could alter which catalog is initially active when users open a new Databricks session.
accepted_impacts.llm_uncertainty: No constructor source details or downstream entrypoint were surfaced, so the exact initialization change is unknown.
accepted_impacts.behavior_label: default catalog selection for new Databricks sessions

pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: Databricks now creates a specialized execution context that discovers, tracks, resolves, and propagates the active catalog. Fresh contexts query the database for CURRENT_CATALOG(), while contexts initialized from another context attempt to adopt its default catalog. Catalog-selection and discovery failures are logged rather than propagated in several paths.

behavior_changes.description: When the Databricks data source creates an execution context, callers now receive a Databricks-specific context with active-catalog tracking rather than the generic execution-context implementation.
evidence: The data source factory now constructs DatabricksExecutionContext directly.

citations.quoted_text: public JDBCExecutionContext createExecutionContext(JDBCRemoteInstance instance, String type) {

behavior_changes.description: A newly initialized Databricks context refreshes its defaults by querying the connected database for its current catalog. A non-empty result becomes the context's tracked catalog and, when bootstrap settings are in use and contain no default catalog, is copied into those settings.
evidence: The no-source initialization path invokes refreshDefaults with bootstrap settings enabled.
refreshDefaults executes SELECT CURRENT_CATALOG(), records a non-empty result, and fills an empty bootstrap default.

behavior_changes.description: A Databricks context initialized from another context now attempts to select the source context's default catalog, so related contexts can begin in the same catalog when that catalog is available.
evidence: The initialization path reads the source context's default catalog and applies it to the new context when non-null.

behavior_changes.description: If changing the default catalog fails with DBCException, the new Databricks context logs the failure and returns normally instead of reporting the failure to its caller.
evidence: The override catches DBCException raised by the superclass operation and does not rethrow it.

important_symbols.reason: It routes all execution-context creation through the new Databricks-specific behavior.
It distinguishes fresh contexts from contexts initialized from an existing one and determines whether catalog state is discovered or copied.
It crosses the JDBC boundary, discovers CURRENT_CATALOG(), and may mutate bootstrap defaults.
It applies catalog selection and changes the superclass exception contract by suppressing DBCException.
It resolves the tracked server catalog name through the data-source catalog model and controls what callers see as the default catalog.

investigation_hints.description: Trace execution-context construction and initialization to determine which connection, metadata, editor, and auxiliary-context lifecycles use the new context and whether initFrom is always Databricks-specific.

Inspect catalog-selection semantics across the superclass, JDBC driver, and Databricks server, including whether CURRENT_CATALOG() is supported in all relevant modes and whether catalog objects are loaded before name-based resolution.
Determine the ownership and persistence semantics of bootstrap settings because refreshDefaults writes a server-observed catalog into that object when its default is empty.
Review callers' expectations for DBCException from setDefaultCatalog and whether continuing after a failed catalog switch can execute later work in an unintended catalog.

local_risks.description: A failed catalog switch is hidden from the caller. If subsequent work assumes the requested catalog was selected, it can operate against the previously active catalog without receiving the declared DBCException; this is a material correctness risk for catalog-qualified state and queries.

local_risks.description: Once activeCatalogName is non-empty, default-catalog lookup no longer falls back to the superclass result; it returns only the data source's name-based catalog lookup. If the server-reported catalog is absent from the loaded catalog model, callers may observe no default catalog despite a usable superclass default.

affected_boundaries.label: Databricks execution-context catalog lifecycle
evidence: The createExecutionContext source returns `new DatabricksExecutionContext(instance, type)` as a `JDBCExecutionContext`.
The established call edge `createExecutionContext` -> `DatabricksExecutionContext` is recorded in DatabricksDataSource.java at line 97.
The established call edges from `initializeContextState` to `getDefaultCatalog`, `refreshDefaults`, and `setDefaultCatalog` are recorded in DatabricksDataSource.java at line 81.
The `refreshDefaults` source opens a JDBC session and executes a query to discover the current catalog, while `setDefaultCatalog` delegates catalog selection and updates `activeCatalogName`.
The `getDefaultCatalog` source exposes the tracked catalog through the execution-context catalog contract, falling back to the superclass implementation when no active catalog is tracked.
affected_boundaries.reason: The data-source lifecycle crosses into the specialized Databricks execution-context domain surface to construct contexts and initialize, read, refresh, or change their catalog state.
